<reason>CON won a competitive clash by forcing the live choice onto a well-behaved nightly companion and showing PRO’s extra duties (overnight limits, session friction) still attach after anti-manipulation and healthy-disengagement design are satisfied. PRO had the stickier frame—social occupation, leftover product after slogans, presence-as-pressure—but treated the friend-role as self-justifying and never showed why those extra restrictions protect better than CON’s pre-release mechanism test. CON answered the “waiting for harm” charge directly and made over-inclusion the easier vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>After PRO conceded the good hypo still gets classified, CON’s access-versus-inducement reply (a sleep-encouraging bot is not a prolongation machine) turned overnight friction into unjustified over-inclusion rather than child protection.</best_rebuttal>
